The answer to your question is:

When you have "excact" distance data (ie don't specify intervals in Data

Filter | Intervals tab) then by default Distance selects 3 sets of=20
intervals

(few, some, many) to calculate chi-sq gof stats for. Remember this doesnt

change the fit at all - just the way the data are presented. So all 3 plo=
ts

have the same fit and parameter values, just different chi sq values. For

more on this, see Chapter 8 of the users guide, under Output from CDS

analyses, CDS results details listing. It's almost always better to speci=
fy

intervals for GOF manually, rather than relying on the defaults -- see th=
e

CDS analysis guidelines in that chapter. Also, to get an overall impressi=
on

of goodness of fit, I prefer to look at the Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Craeme=
r-

vonMises tests (see also Chapter 8) as these don't require the data to be

put into arbitrary bins to calculate the test statistics.

Hope this helps,

- len

Those are all the same fitted graph. The only thing that changes is

the binning of the histograms to represent the data.

--jeff

Megan:

Those figures are all depictions of the same detection function, but=20
using finer and finer binning of your data. The chi-squared test=20
statistic changes with each depiction because the binning of 'observed'=20
and 'expected' changes. That is one of the difficulties of the=20
chi-squared goodness of fit test; you have continuous detection=20
distances, but they are converted into discrete ranges for the purposes=20
of performing the test (section 3.4.4 of the Buckland et al.(2001)).

Because you have continuous distance measurements, the=20
Kolomogorov-Smirnov and the Cramer-Von Mises tests are probably more=20
informative (see section 11.11 of Buckland et al.(2004)). They are=20
designed to operate on continuous data, and hence do not need to go=20
through the process of invoking cut-points upon your data. So the best=20
solution is study the K-S and C-VM test results; the chi-square goodness=20
of fit figures are visual depictions of your data for your inspection.

Eric
